ranking.name: Air temperature near the ground
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, air temperature near the ground in Antarctica changed by +0.249 °C per decade (95% confidence interval +0.195 to +0.304), which is statistically significant (p < 0.001). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.615 °C.

ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in Antarctica shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.99): the estimate is 0.000 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.018 to +0.017). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.

ranking.name: Water leaving the land (evapotranspiration)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, there is no trend estimate for water leaving the land (evapotranspiration) in Antarctica: this variable is only available over land, and no land cell in this region has enough data.
